title: Bald Cypress: Ancient Swamp Cypresses You Can Visit
meta_description: A swamp tree from the American South. Old Baldy in Austin was already old when a Franciscan friar wrote about it in 1716.
intro: Bald cypress grows with its feet in standing water in the swamps of the American South, pushing woody knees up out of the mud around its trunk, and it is a conifer that drops its needles every autumn. At home it lives for centuries. Old Baldy, on Onion Creek in Austin, was already old when Father Antonio Olivares wrote about it in 1716, and Texas puts it past five hundred years. Abroad, nineteenth century gardeners wanted the shape and took the swamp tree without the swamp. Berlin's has stood for two centuries in the Charlottenburg palace garden. Seville built its monument to the poet Becquer around one that was growing on the spot first. Miyazaki Shrine holds the largest in Japan, and Milan's was filed under the wrong genus for years until somebody checked properly.
